heading.en: The racing car that changes its note

hook.en: Stand beside a road as a motorbike roars past: its note is high as it comes and drops the moment it passes. The engine has not changed; what you hear has.

objectives.en: State the Doppler effect for sound
Explain why a moving source changes the wavelength

narration.en: Stand beside a road as a motorbike roars past: its note is high as it comes and drops the moment it passes. The engine has not changed; what you hear has.

title.en: Crowded waves in front, stretched waves behind

body.en: A source of frequency f sends out one crest every 1/f second. If it moves at $v_s$ towards the listener, each new crest starts $v_s/f$ closer than the last, so the wavelength ahead is $\lambda' = (v - v_s)/f$. The speed of sound $v$ is fixed by the air, so the listener hears $f' = v/\lambda' = f\,\dfrac{v}{v - v_s}$. Moving away, the sign changes: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v}{v + v_s}$.

points.en: The speed of sound does not change
Ahead of the source: shorter λ, higher pitch
Behind it: longer λ, lower pitch

narration.en: A source of frequency f sends out one crest every 1/f second. If it moves at $v_s$ towards the listener, each new crest starts $v_s/f$ closer than the last, so the wavelength ahead is $\lambda' = (v - v_s)/f$. The speed of sound $v$ is fixed by the air, so the listener hears $f' = v/\lambda' = f\,\dfrac{v}{v - v_s}$. Moving away, the sign changes: $f' = f\,\dfrac{v}{v + v_s}$.
Each circle is a crest. When the source moves, the circles are no longer centred on the same point. Crests ahead come closer together, so the listener ahead hears a higher note.

caption.en: Each circle is a crest sent out once a second. Raise the source speed (as a fraction of the speed of sound) and see the crests crowd together in front and spread out behind.

tryThis.en: Set the source speed to 0. Are the crests equally spaced everywhere?
Set it to 0.5. Compare the spacing ahead and behind.
At 0.9, what would happen near the speed of sound?

title.en: Deriving f′ for a moving source

say.en: In one period T the first crest travels v T. The source travels v s T towards the listener.
The next crest starts from the new position, so the gap between crests is v T minus v s T.
The sound still travels at v, so f prime equals v over lambda prime.

aim.en: To find the speed of sound in air, which is the v in every Doppler formula.

narration.en: Optional lab: find the speed of sound in air with a resonance tube. Every Doppler formula uses this speed v.

points.en: The Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency due to motion of the source or the listener.
A moving source changes the wavelength: f′ = f v/(v − v_s) approaching, f v/(v + v_s) receding.
The speed of sound depends only on the medium.

homework.en: A 400 Hz whistle moves away from you at 40 m/s (v = 340 m/s). What do you hear? (Answer: about 358 Hz)

narration.en: Recap. The Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency due to motion of the source or the listener. A moving source changes the wavelength: f′ = f v/(v − v_s) approaching, f v/(v + v_s) receding. The speed of sound depends only on the medium.
